codeReview.summary: The implementation fully satisfies the feature requirements: pure domain types in internal/platform/worktree/ with Manager interface, all required structs (WorktreeEntry, WorktreeResult, WorktreeStatus, CreateOptions, RemoveOptions, CopyOptions, HookConfig), and functional option functions. The code follows the functional core / imperative shell pattern — no IO, no external imports beyond stdlib (context, time). The package is well-documented with doc.go, thorough godoc on all public types and methods, and 36 comprehensive unit tests covering all types, options, conversions, edge cases (detached HEAD, bare repos, zero values, last-wins semantics).

sharedStateObservations.observation: The functional options pattern used here (unified Options struct with WithXxx option functions converting to typed CreateOpts/RemoveOpts/CopyOpts) is a clean pattern that could be useful for other packages. It's consistent with the existing protocol.Option pattern in the codebase but adds the typed conversion layer. No gap — just noting the consistency.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: internal/platform/worktree/types.go — Option func(*Options), Options.CreateOpts()/RemoveOpts()/CopyOpts() methods; compare internal/protocol/protocol.go Option pattern

sharedStateObservations.observation: The Manager interface comment references `git worktree list --porcelain` output format. The porcelain format specifics (field names: 'worktree', 'HEAD', 'branch', 'bare', 'locked', 'prunable') are documented in the godoc but not in .factory/library/. Future workers implementing the adapter will need these porcelain format details. Currently the knowledge is embedded in code comments which is adequate for this types-only feature.
